title: Linear dip motion gives no median forecast gain in released TESS models of 91 CPV stars
abstract: We test whether constant motion of Gaussian dip centers predicts later shapes of complex periodic variables. We use 9,036 released TESS windows from 178 visits to 91 stars. Geometry is fitted on the first two thirds of each visit and frozen for the last third. Both fixed and moving models have free nonnegative dip depths in each window. The median error reduction across stars is -0.11%, with a 95% star-bootstrap interval of -1.60% to +1.30%. Motion lowers training error by 3.11% at the median, but gives no clear median later-window gain. Successful fits, interior speeds and a training-error cut give the same null result. Ideal synthetic moving patterns give gains in 24 of 24 cases, while fixed patterns give gains in 4 of 24. The tested model has limited predictive value beyond depth changes. This does not exclude material motion. The source period uses the full visit, the Gaussian family is restricted, and the synthetic drift is larger than many reported drifts. The result is conditional on released summaries, not a blind raw-data forecast. Code, aggregate results, two figures, source hashes and reproduction steps are included.
